name: Franks Casket
description: The Franks Casket, also called the Auzon Casket, is an eighth-century Anglo-Saxon chest carved from whalebone, about 23 centimetres long, with panels bearing scenes from Germanic legend, the Bible and classical history, framed by inscriptions in runes and Latin. Its front panel shows the smith Weland being released by the maiden Beadohild after his imprisonment by King Nithhad, while the right panel shows the Adoration of the Magi, a pairing of pagan and Christian imagery typical of the period. The runic inscriptions, including a cryptic challenge in Old English verse, make the casket one of the most studied objects in early English archaeology. It was bought in the nineteenth century by the antiquarian Augustus Franks after being found at Auzon in France, and is now in the British Museum, with one panel in the Bargello in Florence. The casket's mixture of whalebone, runes and interwoven legends marks it as a key witness to Anglo-Saxon storytelling.
